data.name: Asalatha
data.gender_notes: Asalatha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asalatha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'asala', meaning pure or ethereal. In Hindu mythology, Asalatha is the name of a celestial nymph or aethereal woman, symbolizing purity and divinity. The name Asalatha carries the meaning “Pure, Ethereal, Divine” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Asalatha usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, ethereal, divine and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A divine embodiment of purity and grace

data.cultural_impact: Asalatha is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture, representing a transcendent and ethereal beauty. Its use has been popularized in various texts and stories, most notably in the ancient Sanskrit epic, the Mahabharata. Here, Asalatha, or AhалTlett, is mentioned as one of the Kaurava princesses and is also the name of a celestial nymph, making her an embodiment of both royal and divine grace.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Asalatha holds immense spiritual significance as a reminder of living a pure and pious life. The prefix 'asala' in the name signifies purity and ethereality, making Asalatha synonymous with the divine feminine. In Hinduism, the feminine represents Shakti, or divine energy, which is believed to pervade the universe. Thus, Asalatha represents the sacred connection we all have to the divine, and serves as an inspiration for maintaining a pure heart and mind on our spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Asalatha was a famous Vedic Rishi, revered for her wisdom and learning. She is believed to have authored many hymns in the Rigveda, and is mentioned in several Puranas.

Asalatha is also known as one of the 18 Maharshis or great sages, who were believed to have lived during the Treta Yuga. She is considered a manifestation of Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of wisdom and knowledge.
